proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1 and a real number t with (n-1)/n <= t < 1. Let k be any integer with 1 <= k <= n. We show that floor(k t) = k-1.

From t < 1 we get k t < k.
From t >= (n-1)/n we get
k t >= k(n-1)/n = k - k/n.
Since k <= n, we have k/n <= 1, hence k - k/n >= k - 1. Therefore
k - 1 <= k t < k.

Because k-1 is an integer and it is the greatest integer not exceeding k t, it follows that floor(k t) = k-1.

Since k was arbitrary, this holds for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n.
solver_summary: For k in {1,...,n}, the bounds (n-1)/n <= t < 1 imply k-1 <= kt < k, so the floor is exactly k-1.
vetter_reason: The proof establishes the required bounds k-1 <= k*t < k for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n, and concludes correctly that floor(k*t) = k-1. This exactly matches the lemma statement, with no semantic drift and no dependency issues.
